title: Thursday's page
how: Three picks. One tap each; a note is optional. Your picks save on the page.
foot: Anything you do not pick carries onto the next page.

sections.name: The voice's delay: down from 4 s to 3 s for a short line in the game, but every faster way I built runs at half speed beside the game. What next?
sections.note: Measured in the finished game, 1 October. The voice's work for a short line (1.6 s of speech): 3.95 s before, 2.98 s now (its decoder moved to the graphics card, same sound). On the real path the words come at 1.9 s (30 lines, 30 September), so the first sound is now about 4.5 s after Enter, covered by the characters' short sounds. Tried tonight and failed in the game: making the voice in pieces inside the sentence (1.0 s to the first piece on the idle PC, but beside the game each piece took 1.5 s, so replies came slower with gaps); a compiled version of the voice's main loop (92 steps a second idle, 17 beside the game, against 25 today); a 60 and a 30 frame cap, half the picture's resolution, and a higher priority for the voice: none changed it. Beside the running game every way runs at about half its idle speed. The one lead left: the voice inside the game itself with its own high priority on the graphics card, which a separate program cannot have. Unproven; I would research it first. Moving the voice into the game is already on the road to release (about two weeks by the earlier note), since a friend's PC should not need Python. The rest of this week's list: mouths, nightly tests of the finished game, Mickey's office, filming the suit jacket (the friends' build waits on the fresh Windows account).
options: This week's other items first, then research and move the voice into the game (recommended)
Research and move the voice into the game now; the other items wait
Leave the voice as it is for now

sections.name: Ron's "Well now.": which face looks like him saying it?
sections.detail: Filmed in the game from 60 cm, the same sound twice in a row in the same place: one face is Epic's tool reading the sound, the other follows its loudness, as all speech in play does today. Which is which is kept off the page. The film is ten frames a second, so it moves coarsely; the game is smooth. A blind reviewer's notes: A: the mouth opens in the first half only and stays shut for "now"; his eyes are half-lidded, looking down to his right. B: the upper face is frozen and only the jaw drops, with no rounding for "w" or "ow".

sections.name: Darren's "Hmm. Well now.": which face looks like him saying it?
sections.detail: Filmed in the game from 60 cm, the same sound twice in a row in the same place: one face is Epic's tool reading the sound, the other follows its loudness, as all speech in play does today. Which is which is kept off the page. The film is ten frames a second, so it moves coarsely; the game is smooth. A blind reviewer's notes: A: the lips part during "Hmm", and spread rather than round on "Well". B: still for the first 0.6 s, and "Well now" comes in one small opening.
